Theorem
[Perron solution] 1. ch6:6.11\group gt-ch06 If $c\le 0$, the coefficients and $f$ are locally $C^\alpha $, and the above supremum is bounded, then $u\in C^{2,\alpha }(\Omega )$ and $Lu=f$ in $\Omega $.
Proof

\sketch Solve on balls, use stability of subsolutions and the interior compactness from Corollary 6.3, and apply the strong maximum principle.

□

At a boundary point $x_0$ where $\varphi $ is continuous, an upper (lower) barrier is a sequence of superfunctions (subfunctions) $w_i^\pm $ with $w_i^\pm (x_0)\to \varphi (x_0)$. A barrier means both sequences.
